title: Audit Log & Data Handling: GTM Messaging Brief
content:
Context and purpose:
This is a working draft aimed at aligning product, legal, and GTM on concise, defensible language we can use in sales decks, website security pages, and one-pagers for regulated customers. Focus areas: SOC2/ISO/ISO27001/HIPAA readiness claims, data handling bullets (what we collect, how we store, inference-data residency), and audit-log / observability language that sales can cite without overpromising.

Audience:
- Sales & Solutions Engineers (battlecards, discovery questions)
- Product Marketing (website, datasheets)
- Legal & Compliance (claim sign-off)

TL;DR recommended high-level claims (short, safe):
- "SOC 2 Type II: Redwood Inference maintains SOC 2 Type II controls covering our hosted control plane and operational practices — reports available under NDA for qualified customers."
- "ISO-aligned security program: Our security program follows ISO 27001 principles; certification workstreams are documented and available to partners on request."
- "HIPAA-ready options: For customers requiring HIPAA protections, Redwood offers Private deployments (VPC / on-prem) and Business Associate Agreements — with audit logging and access controls configured per customer requirements."
- "Data minimization & controls: We do not use customer data to train models. Customers can choose hosted, dedicated, or private deployments to meet data residency and isolation needs."

What sales can say (copy-friendly bullets):
- "We provide industry-standard controls (SOC 2 Type II) and maintain evidence packages for enterprise review under NDA."
- "Audit logs capture request metadata, model and model version, timestamps, request and response sizes, and operator actions — configurable retention up to X days in hosted plans and unlimited under Dedicated/Private contracts."
- "Private deployments allow customers to retain full control of PII/PHI and integrate with their KMS/HSM for encryption-at-rest keys."
- "We support per-route entitlements and tracing hooks for incident investigations and third-party audits."

What to avoid / do not claim:
- Do not say we are "HIPAA certified" or that SOC 2 covers customer-managed private deployments unless legal has explicitly approved the wording.
- Avoid unbounded retention promises (e.g., "we store logs forever") — use configurable retention ranges.

Audit-log recommended language (detailed):
- "Audit logging: Redwood records a tamper-evident audit trail for API requests and control-plane actions. Logs include request ID, timestamp (UTC), caller identity (API key or user id), model and model version, token counts, routing decision, and error codes. For hosted customers, default retention is 90 days; Dedicated customers can request extended retention up to 2 years; Private deployments are configured per contract."
- "Log integrity: Logs are append-only and cryptographically time-stamped in our log pipeline; export and S3 archival are available for customers with longer retention needs and for compliance evidence."
- "Access and governance: Only authorized personnel with role-based access can view raw audit logs; access is audited and requires justification logged in the ticketing system."

Data handling / privacy bullets (plain language):
- "We do not use customer-provided prompt or response data to improve public models or our model catalog without explicit opt-in."
- "Hosted API: transient KV caching and prefix caching may be enabled to optimize latency; cache lifetimes are documented and can be disabled upon request."
- "Encryption: Data in transit is always encrypted (TLS 1.2+). Data at rest is encrypted using customer-managed keys for Private deployments and our managed KMS for hosted plans; Dedicated offers KMS peering."
- "Residency: Customers can choose routing policies to keep inference in specific regions; Private deployments provide full on-prem / VPC residency."

Competitive callouts (how others frame it):
- OpenAI / Anthropic style: emphasize secure-by-default hosted platform and SOC2; customers often ask about BAA availability — OpenAI positions BAAs for select enterprise customers.
- AWS/Azure: push the cloud provider compliance pedigree (PCI/HIPAA/ISO) and hardware flexibility; their messaging is broad but less focused on LLM inference economics.
- Cohere / Mistral: tend to emphasize model governance and data usage transparency.

Positioning recommendation vs competition:
- Lead with "inference that meets your compliance needs" — highlight deployment options (hosted, dedicated, private) as the core differentiator.
- Emphasize operational observability: we expose token-level billing, audit trails, and model-versioned responses which makes forensic/regression investigations easier than just handing raw model outputs to customers.
- Stress contract-level controls: BAAs, extended retention, and SLA-backed options for Dedicated customers.

GTM artifacts to create (quick list / priorities):
1) Sales one-pager: "Security & Compliance: How Redwood protects customer data" (single page, pull-quotes: SOC2, BAA, audit logs, private deploy).
2) Battlecard for SEs: likely objections + recommended responses + sample discovery questions (PII/PHI, residency, retention, audit trails).
3) Website security page draft: shorter customer-facing bits + link to compliance kit request form.
4) Internal FAQ for legal/product to sign off on exact phrasing that sales can use.

Sample SE discovery questions (for call):
- "What categories of data will you send to the model (PII/PHI/IP)?"
- "Do you need a BAA or are you evaluating Dedicated/Private options?"
- "How long must audit logs be retained for your compliance/audit needs?"
- "Do you require customer-managed encryption keys or on-prem deployments?"

Draft battlecard lines (short responses):
- Objection: "How can I be sure you don't train on our data?"
  Response: "We do not use customer prompts/responses to train public models without explicit opt-in; Private deployments give you complete isolation and full control over data flow."
- Objection: "We need HIPAA — can Redwood do that?"
  Response: "Yes — we offer HIPAA-ready configurations via Private deployments and BAAs; our SEs can map a compliance checklist to your controls during POC."

Open questions / decisions to resolve with Legal/Product:
- Exact hosted audit-log default retention value for marketing (90 days?) — confirm and lock wording.
- Can we publicly state "SOC 2 Type II" vs. only provide under NDA? Clarify with legal on where and how to assert compliance.
- Is the phrase "we do not train on customer data" safe for all hosted plans or only for customers with explicit opt-out/contract?

Next actions / owners:
- Legal: finalize acceptable phrasing for public site + NDA gating (owner: Priya Rao)
- Product: confirm hosted default retention and caching opt-out (owner: Diego Morales)
- Solutions Eng: build slide deck snippets and sample config templates for Private/HIPAA POC (owner: Liam O'Reilly)

Notes to self / rough text snippets for website (editable):
- "Security & Compliance at a glance: SOC 2 Type II controls, ISO-aligned security program, and configurable deployments for regulated workloads. Reports and configurations available to enterprise customers under NDA."
- "Audit Logs: Request-level, model-versioned audit trails retain caller identity and routing decisions. Exportable archives for third-party audits and e-discovery."

References / useful links (internal):
- Confluence: Audit retention policy (linked above)
- Jira: JIRA-1245 (request: add audit-log export to S3)
- Docs PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/432 (draft audit log API)
